headline: Wanted: an assistant. Quick, keen, sometimes makes things up.
notes: Style 07 relatable, format F6 the honest job advert, cheatsheet card. Joke: the job advert shape. Lesson: what to hand it, what to give it, what never to trust or hand it. Link: you judge a new hire by exactly these lines. Alt text: A job advert for an AI assistant: hire it for first drafts of the emails you put off; on its first morning tell it who it is for, what happened and what good looks like; never trust it with a price, date or measurement you have not checked; never hand it customer names or bank details; always check every number against the original.

headline: Turn a 30-email thread into 3 lines

notes: Style 05 carousel, eight slides, sequence: a long thread to three lines. Destination /prompts opened 1 November 2026. Alt text: An eight-slide guide: copy the whole email thread, take the private details out, type the words on slide 4 asking for what has been decided, what you are being asked and by when, paste the thread underneath, and check the date and the ask against the original emails.

headline: Three changes in Gemini and Copilot worth a try
notes: Style 06 roundup. Items: Google 29 Oct https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/create-preview-and-edit-files-directly-in-the-Gemini-app.html ; Google 30 Oct https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/edit-entire-presentations-with-Gemini-in-Google-Slides.html ; Microsoft 27 Oct https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/release-notes (Reference an attached PowerPoint deck's style, roadmap 555879, plan not stated). No ChatGPT item: the ChatGPT release notes page could not be read this run, and openai.com/products/release-notes showed nothing after 4 June 2026. Rejected: Fill with Gemini citations (a, Standard and Plus only, minor), pivot compact layout (c), immersive explorations (c), classic Outlook Copilot settings (c), Notebooks items (c), Learning Agent (a, plan unclear), Canva in Researcher (a). Alt text: Three changes worth trying. Gemini: the Gemini app now makes a document, sheet or slides in the chat on Workspace and personal Google accounts; ask for a price list as a sheet. Google Slides: on Business Standard or Plus one request can update a whole deck; ask Gemini to change every date. PowerPoint: if Copilot shows, it can copy the look of a deck you attach.

headline: What we type, and what the assistant needed to know
notes: Style 07 relatable, format F2 what we all type and what works, beforeafter card. Joke: six words in, a vague email out. Lesson: type the context already in your head. Link: the gap between the two IS the lesson. Alt text: Before and after. What we all type: write an email to the supplier. What gets a usable answer: write an email to the supplier about the delivery due on a date that has not arrived, ask for a new date by Friday and say what we need it for, under 80 words, firm not rude, and write CHECK where you do not know something.

headline: 38% of UK businesses had a phishing attack in the last 12 months
notes: Style 03 stat, hook formula 4 (plain count). Figure sentence: Phishing attacks remained the most prevalent type of breach or attack by far (experienced by 38% of businesses and 25% of charities). Supporting, same document: micro (42%) and small (46%) any breach or attack. Sample 2,112 UK businesses, August to December 2025, Ipsos for DSIT and the Home Office; official statistics. Opened 1 November 2026. Alt text: A stat card: 38% of UK businesses had a phishing attack in the last 12 months, the most common attack by far. Agree one rule this week: any email asking to change bank details gets a call to a number you already have.
